policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the SBLGNT reading.

decisions.evidence: ASV reads 'there were at Antioch, in the church that was there, prophets and teachers' with no indefinite 'certain'; the added τινες of r01 would be rendered 'certain prophets and teachers'.
The variant is only the article on 'the Lord'; ASV 'ministered to the Lord' renders either reading identically.
ASV 'So they, being sent forth' renders the personal pronoun αὐτοί; the demonstrative οὗτοι of r01 would appear as 'these'.
Word order and article only; both readings yield ASV 'the Holy Spirit'.
Article before the place name is invisible in ASV 'went down to Seleucia'.
τε and δὲ are both carried by ASV 'and from thence they sailed'; the English does not distinguish the connective.
Article before the place name is invisible in ASV 'sailed to Cyprus'.
ASV 'when they had gone through the whole island' renders ὅλην, which r01 omits.

ASV 'a certain sorcerer' shows no separate 'man', but ASV regularly collapses ἀνήρ with an appositional noun (cf. ἄνδρα φονέα rendered 'a murderer'), so the English does not settle whether ἄνδρα stood.
The variant is only the case ending of the name; ASV 'whose name was Bar-Jesus' renders either form.
ASV 'filled with the Holy Spirit, fastened his eyes on him' joins the participles without a conjunction; the added καὶ of r01 would surface as 'and fastened his eyes on him'.
The variant is the article on κυρίου; ASV 'the right ways of the Lord' renders either reading.
δὲ and τε are both covered by ASV 'And now, behold'; the mapped note is classed alternative_rendering and concerns 'until', not this connective.
Simple and compound aorist alike give ASV 'there fell on him', the ἐπὶ being carried by the following ἐπ᾽ αὐτόν in both readings.
Article within οἱ περὶ Παῦλον; ASV 'Paul and his company' renders either reading.
ASV 'Antioch of Pisidia' renders the genitive τῆς Πισιδίας; the base accusative attributive τὴν Πισιδίαν would give 'Pisidian Antioch'.
ASV 'they went into the synagogue' suits both the compound εἰσελθόντες and ἐλθόντες with εἰς.
ASV 'if ye have any word of exhortation' renders τίς; r01 omits it and would read simply 'if there is a word'.
Word order only; ASV 'if ye have any word of exhortation' renders either arrangement.
ASV 'The God of this people Israel' renders Ἰσραήλ, which r01 omits.
ASV 'in the land of Egypt' is the ordinary rendering of both the genitive Αἰγύπτου and the appositional dative Αἰγύπτῳ.
ASV opens the sentence 'And when he had destroyed seven nations', rendering the connective καὶ that r01 omits.
ASV 'he gave them their land for an inheritance' has an indirect object that English idiom requires with 'gave', so it does not show whether αὐτοῖς stood in the Greek.

ASV puts 'for about four hundred and fifty years' at the close of v19 and begins v20 'and after these things he gave them judges', the order of r01; r02 would read 'and after that he gave them judges about the space of four hundred and fifty years'.
Article on προφήτου only; ASV 'until Samuel the prophet' renders either reading.
Word order only; ASV 'he raised up David to be their king' renders either arrangement.
ASV 'brought unto Israel a Saviour, Jesus' names the person; r01's σωτηρίαν would read 'salvation'.
ASV 'to all the people of Israel' renders παντί, which r01 lacks.
Article on the personal name; ASV 'as John was fulfilling his course' renders either reading.
ASV 'What suppose ye that I am?' renders the neuter τί; r01's τίνα με would give 'Whom think ye that I am?'
ASV 'to us is the word of this salvation sent forth' renders the first person ἡμῖν, not ὑμῖν.
ASV 'sent forth' serves both the compound ἐξαπεστάλη and simple ἀπεστάλη, which ASV also renders 'send forth'.
ASV 'who are now his witnesses unto the people' renders νῦν, which r01 omits.
ASV 'hath fulfilled the same unto our children' renders τοῖς τέκνοις ἡμῶν; r01 would give 'unto their children, to us'.
ASV 'in the second psalm' excludes Treg's πρώτῳ (r02) but does not distinguish the word order of the base reading from r01.
ASV 'Because he saith also in another psalm' renders causal διότι; r01's διό would give 'Wherefore'.
Article only; ASV 'through this man is proclaimed unto you remission of sins' renders either reading.
ASV 'lest that come upon you which is spoken in the prophets' renders ἐφ᾽ ὑμᾶς, which the base reading lacks.
Word order only; ASV 'For I work a work in your days' renders either arrangement.
ASV repeats the noun in 'A work which ye shall in no wise believe', rendering ἔργον, which r01 omits.
ASV 'And as they went out' has neither 'out of the synagogue' (r01) nor 'out of the synagogue of the Jews' (r02).
ASV 'they besought' supplies no subject; r01's added τὰ ἔθνη would read 'the Gentiles besought'.
ASV 'that these words might be spoken to them' renders ταῦτα, which r01 omits.
ASV 'who, speaking to them, urged them' renders the dative αὐτοῖς with the participle, which r01 omits.
ASV 'to continue in the grace of God' renders either compound of μένειν.
δὲ and τε alike are covered by ASV 'And the next sabbath'; the mapped textual note concerns κυρίου/θεοῦ, not this connective.
ASV text reads 'to hear the word of God' with the mapped textual_variant note 'Many ancient authorities read the Lord', so θεοῦ stands in the text and κυρίου is the noted alternative.
Article on Παύλου; ASV 'spoken by Paul' renders either reading.
ASV 'the things which were spoken' renders either λαλουμένοις or λεγομένοις; the mapped note is alternative_rendering and concerns 'railed'.
ASV has a single 'contradicted' followed by 'and blasphemed'; r01's ἀντιλέγοντες καὶ βλασφημοῦντες would add a second contradicting participle.
τε and δὲ alike are covered by ASV 'And Paul and Barnabas spake out boldly'.
ASV begins the sentence 'Seeing ye thrust it from you' with no adversative; r01's added δὲ would give 'But seeing ye thrust it from you'.
Singular and plural verb with neuter plural τὰ ἔθνη alike give ASV 'they were glad'.
ASV text reads 'glorified the word of God' with the mapped textual_variant note 'Many ancient authorities read the Lord', so θεοῦ stands in the text.
ASV 'the devout women of honorable estate' has no conjunction between the two attributives; r01's added καὶ would give 'the devout and honorable women'.
Article only; ASV 'and the chief men of the city' renders either reading.
ASV 'the dust of their feet' supplies a possessive that ASV regularly gives to an articular body part, so the English does not show whether αὐτῶν stood.
τε and δὲ alike are covered by ASV 'And the disciples were filled with joy'.
